Note::transpose¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::transpose(std::int64_t dim0, std::int64_t dim1) const

Swap Two Axes¶

transpose() returns a Note with axes dim0 and dim1 exchanged and all other axes left where they are. On a 2 × 3 grid, transpose(0, 1) gives the 3 × 2 grid whose rows are the original columns. It is the short form of the common case that permute covers in general — a.transpose(i, j) is exactly a.permute(p) where p is the identity with i and j swapped.

Like permute, transpose moves cells: the offset table is rebuilt so that a row-major read of the result walks the cells in transposed order. The cell strings are shared with the source (no copy, no re-encode), the bytes-vs-UTF-8 mode carries over, and the cost is one O(numel) pass.

The argument contract¶

  • Both dim0 and dim1 must be in [0, dim()) — a value outside that range raises transpose dim out of range. There is no negative-axis form.

  • dim0 == dim1 is allowed and returns the Note unchanged.

  • On a 1-D Note the only valid call is transpose(0, 0); on a 0-D Note every call raises transpose dim out of range (there are no axes to address).

Example 1: The 2-D Transpose¶

const auto m = pluss::make_note({{"a", "b", "c"}, {"d", "e", "f"}});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(m.transpose(0, 1)) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3, 2], dim=2, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a", "d"], 
  ["b", "e"], 
  ["c", "f"]
]

Example 2: Swapping The Outer And Inner Axis Of A Rank-3 Note¶

const auto t = pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"}).reshape({1, 2, 3});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(t.transpose(0, 2)) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3, 2, 1], dim=3, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
[
  [
    ["a"], 
    ["d"]
  ], 
  [
    ["b"], 
    ["e"]
  ], 
  [
    ["c"], 
    ["f"]
  ]
]

The middle axis (size 2) stays put; the size-1 and size-3 axes trade places.

Example 3: No-Op Forms¶

const auto m = pluss::make_note({{"a", "b", "c"}, {"d", "e", "f"}});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(m.transpose(1, 1)) << "\n";   // same axis twice

const auto v = pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(v.transpose(0, 0)) << "\n";   // 1-D

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 3], dim=2, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a", "b", "c"], 
  ["d", "e", "f"]
]
Note(shape=[6], dim=1, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
["a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"]

Example 4: Out-Of-Range Axis¶

try {
  (void)pluss::make_note({"a", "b"}).transpose(0, 1);
} catch (const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

transpose dim out of range

The Note is rank 1, so axis 1 does not exist.

See Also¶

  • Note::permute: reorder three axes at once, or apply any permutation.

  • Note::reshape: regroup the same cells without moving them.
